newsitem.title: GERMANY: German steel workers block traffic in Dortmund.
newsitem.headline: German steel workers block traffic in Dortmund.

text.p: Around 200 angry steel workers carrying placards and banners to protest against thousands of job cuts brought traffic at a major intersection to a halt in the city of Dortmund on Thursday.

Steel workers allowed local trams to pass but otherwise blocked traffic for around an hour as local police looked on before the demonstrators got up and made their way to the Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG steel works.

The demonstration was just part of continued protests by thousands of Krupp Hoesch steel workers that has stopped steel production for a week to protest against planned job cuts in the wake of a merger with rival steel maker Thyssen Stahl AG.

The parent companies of the two steel makers, Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and Thyssen AG said on Wednesday they had signed a basic agreement to merge their steel units on April 1 and that 8,000 jobs would be cut.
The steel merger follows an unsuccessful hostile takeover bid for all of Thyssen by its smaller rival Krupp Hoesch.
